planting.note: Plant tubers after last frost, once soil has warmed, in rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade to full sun; Thailand Giant is among the largest-leaved colocasia available and needs abundant water, fertility, and space to reach full size.

directions: Plant tubers after last frost, once soil has warmed, in rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade to full sun; Thailand Giant is among the largest-leaved colocasia available and needs abundant water, fertility, and space to reach full size. Enormous, matte blue-green, heart-shaped leaves can reach four feet or more in length on tall, thick stems, making this one of the largest and most dramatic elephant ears grown, capable of creating an instant jungle effect at the back of a border or beside a pond in a single warm season. Unlike ordinary colocasia grown mainly for foliage, mature plants also occasionally produce large, fragrant, upright white flower spikes reminiscent of a giant peace lily bloom, an unusual bonus for a plant typically valued for leaf size alone. Feed heavily and water generously through the growing season to support its massive leaf production, and in zones colder than 8, lift and store the tuber indoors over winter or grow it as a dramatic single-season annual.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Jacklyn alocasia is frost-tender and best grown as a container specimen moved indoors for winter outside zones 10-11.

directions: Plant divisions or container stock after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Jacklyn alocasia is frost-tender and best grown as a container specimen moved indoors for winter outside zones 10-11. Narrow, elongated, deeply lobed leaves with dramatically undulating, ruffled margins and prominent silvery-white venation give this hybrid a fine, sculptural texture unlike the broader, smoother leaves of most other commonly grown alocasias. Its slender, upright leaf form and eye-catching vein pattern make it a popular specimen among collectors seeking something more textured and refined than standard elephant ear shapes, well suited to a shaded plant grouping where its distinctive silhouette stands out. Provide consistent warmth and high humidity, protect from direct sun which scorches the leaves, and allow the potting mix to dry slightly between waterings to prevent rot at the rhizome.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Bambino alocasia's compact, dwarf size makes it well suited to a windowsill or small container display.

directions: Plant divisions or container stock after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Bambino alocasia's compact, dwarf size makes it well suited to a windowsill or small container display. Small, narrow, dark green, arrow-shaped leaves with pale silvery-green veining grow on a naturally dwarf, compact hybrid that stays well under a foot and a half tall even at maturity, offering the same striking arrow-shaped alocasia silhouette as larger relatives on a scale appropriate for a small pot or tabletop display. Its manageable size makes it one of the more practical alocasia choices for a limited indoor growing space, a terrarium-adjacent shelf, or a mixed shade container where full-sized elephant ears would quickly overwhelm the display. Provide consistent warmth and high humidity, protect from direct sun which scorches the leaves, and allow the potting mix to dry slightly between waterings.
